sections.title: 1. Summary
sections.html: White-blue-black Zombies. Temmet loots every time you attack, and every card you draw pumps your Zombies. Discarded creatures come back as 4/4 Zombie token copies (Hashaton, The Scarab God, God-Pharaoh's Gift, embalm/eternalize). It wins by going wide with buffed Zombie tokens, backed by "drain 1" effects whenever Zombies enter or die.

sections.title: 2. Key cards and combos
sections.html:
No infinite combos (checked on Commander Spellbook). The deck wins through these engines:

  • Temmet, Naktamun's Will (commander): each attack = loot (draw, then discard). The draw gives every Zombie +1/+1. Each card drawn is a separate trigger, so Pull from Tomorrow for X=5 gives Zombies +5/+5 that turn.
  • Hashaton, Scarab's Fist: whenever you discard a creature card, pay {2}{U} to make a tapped 4/4 Zombie token copy of it. The copy keeps the card's abilities, including "when this enters" effects. This is the deck's best engine.
    • Discard outlets that feed it: Temmet's loot, Champion of Wits, Forgotten Creation, Cryptbreaker, Pull from Tomorrow, Gate to the Afterlife, and cycling.
    • Rhet-Tomb Mystic + Hashaton: Mystic gives every creature card in your hand cycling {1}{U}. Cycling counts as discarding, so you can cycle Grave Titan, then pay {2}{U} for a 4/4 Grave Titan copy that still makes two 2/2 Zombies, while drawing a card.
  • Archfiend of Ifnir: every cycle or discard puts a -1/-1 counter on each creature your opponents control. With Temmet's loot plus Rhet-Tomb Mystic it works as a repeatable one-sided board wipe.
  • Lazotep Chancellor: every discard, pay {1} to amass 2. This stacks with Hashaton on the same discard.
  • The Scarab God: drains each opponent for X every upkeep, where X is the number of Zombies you control. It also turns creature cards in any graveyard into 4/4 Zombies. If it dies, it returns to your hand.
  • Maskwood Nexus: makes all your creatures every creature type, so non-Zombies count for Temmet's pump, lords, Scarab God, Prophet of the Scarab and Rot Hulk.
  • Gate to the Afterlife → God-Pharaoh's Gift: once you have 6+ creature cards in your graveyard, sacrifice Gate to fetch Gift straight onto the battlefield, skipping its 7-mana cost. Gift then makes a hasty 4/4 copy of a creature from your graveyard every turn.
  • Anthems: Cemetery Reaper, Lord of the Accursed, Renewed Solidarity, On Wings of Gold (+1/+1 and flying for Zombies and tokens), Eternal Skylord (flying for Zombie tokens).
  • Drains: Corpse Knight, Wayward Servant, Plague Belcher, Bontu's Monument, Gempalm Polluter (cycle it to drain).
  • Card draw: Midnight Reaper and Undead Augur draw when your Zombies die. Prophet of the Scarab draws a pile.

sections.title: 3. Card balance (my count)
sections.html:
• Lands: 39
  • Ramp: 9, all mana rocks and cost reducers (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Commander's Sphere, Dimir Signet, Orzhov Signet, Talisman of Dominance, Talisman of Hierarchy, Crowded Crypt, Bontu's Monument). No land-search ramp.
  • Card draw: about 10 real sources, plus Temmet's loot and many cycling cards.
  • Targeted removal: 9 (Swords to Plowshares, Swift End, Never, Damn, Despark, Cast Out, Angel of Sanctions, Fleshbag Marauder, Archfiend of Ifnir).
  • Board wipes: 2 (Damn when overloaded, Dusk), plus Liliana's −7.
  • Protection: weak. Only Zombie Master's regeneration, Gleaming Overseer (hexproof for Zombie tokens) and Accursed Duneyard. Nothing protects Temmet.
  • Recursion: very strong (Gravecrawler, Dawn, Liliana −3, Rot Hulk, Lost Monarch, Scarab God, Gift, Unholy Grotto, embalm/eternalize).

Compared with a typical baseline (36–38 lands, 10 ramp, 10 draw, 8–10 removal, 2–4 wipes), it is right on target except for protection.

sections.title: 4. Mana curve
sections.html:
Nonland cards by mana value (X counted as 0, split cards by front half): 1: 4 | 2: 18 | 3: 15 | 4: 9 | 5: 8 | 6: 4 | 7+: 2. Average 3.32. The curve is low and smooth, with plenty of 2-drops.

Colored symbols: black 44, white 21, blue 14. Black is the main color. The deck has many white-black and blue-black dual lands, but 3 cycling Deserts and several other lands enter tapped, so it can be slow on turns 1–3.

sections.title: 5. Rules to know
sections.html:
• Temmet's draw trigger fires once per card drawn, so cycling or loots during combat all pump your Zombies.
  • Hashaton / Scarab God / Gift token copies copy the printed card, but as a 4/4 black Zombie. "When this enters" abilities trigger. A copy of a legendary creature you already control triggers the legend rule, and you keep one of the two.
  • Embalm and eternalize are sorcery-speed only. The token has no mana cost, so its mana value is 0. They are activated abilities, not casting, so God-Eternal Oketra and Bontu's Monument don't trigger.
  • Dusk destroys creatures whose power is 3 or more when it resolves. Your Zombies count that power with anthems included, so lords can make Dusk hit your own board.
  • Aftermath (Dawn, Return): the second half can only be cast from your graveyard, and the card is then exiled.
  • Amass: if you control an Army, it gets the counters. Otherwise you create a 0/0 Zombie Army token first. Renewed Solidarity copies of an Army token don't copy its counters, so the copy is 0/0 (or 1/0) and dies right away (CR 704.5f).
  • Zombie Master's swampwalk only works against a player who controls a Swamp, which includes dual lands with the Swamp type.
  • Afflict triggers when the creature becomes blocked, not when it deals damage.
  • Rot Hulk returns Zombies equal to your number of opponents (3 in a 4-player game).
  • Gravecrawler can be cast from your graveyard whenever you control a Zombie. It can't block.
  • The Scarab God returns to hand only if it dies. Exile stops it.

sections.title: 6. Power level
sections.html: No Game Changers, no two-card infinite combos and no mass land denial. It fits Bracket 2 (Core).

sections.title: 7. Weak spots and swaps
sections.html:
Weak spots:

  • No commander protection.
  • No free sacrifice outlet.
  • Relies on your graveyard, so graveyard hate (Bojuka Bog, Rest in Peace) hurts it.
  • Lots of tapped lands.

Swaps (all stay Bracket 2):

  • Accursed Duneyard → Swiftfoot Boots. Protects Temmet. Duneyard is a colorless land in a 3-color deck.
  • Zombie Master → Diregraf Captain. A Zombie lord with deathtouch that drains when your Zombies die, instead of swampwalk that only works against black players.
  • Binding Mummy → Carrion Feeder. A 1-mana Zombie sacrifice outlet that triggers Midnight Reaper, Undead Augur, Plague Belcher and Priest of the Crossing on demand.

Avoid Phyrexian Altar: with Gravecrawler it makes a two-card infinite, which pushes the deck to Bracket 3.

sections.title: 1. Summary
sections.html: Green-blue-red artifacts and energy. Saheeli earns energy whenever you cast artifacts or Artificers. She spends 3 energy each combat to make a hasty 5/5 copy of your best permanent. It ramps hard, collects energy from many sources, and wins with big flyers and Thopter swarms. It can also win with extra combats from Lightning Runner.

sections.title: 2. Key cards and combos
sections.html:
Infinite combos (confirmed on Commander Spellbook):

  • Lightning Runner + Aetherwind Basker (two-card infinite):
    • Setup: you need about 6+ creatures, Basker can't be summoning sick, and neither creature can be blocked and killed.
    • Loop: attack with both. Basker gives 1 energy per creature you control, and Lightning Runner adds 2. Pay 8 to untap everything and get another combat, then repeat for infinite combats and infinite energy.
  • Saheeli + Lightning Runner + Aetherwind Basker: the same loop, but Saheeli copies Basker each combat, so it works with fewer creatures. Saheeli triggers at the start of every combat, extra combats included.
  • Saheeli + Lightning Runner + Peema Aether-Seer: Saheeli copies Peema each combat. The copy gives energy equal to your biggest creature's power, and you need a creature with 9+ power.
  • Aethertide Whale + Nissa, Worldsoul Speaker + Panharmonicon:
    • Loop: cast Whale by paying 8 energy (Nissa's alternative cost). Panharmonicon makes its "enters" trigger happen twice, for 12 energy. Pay 4 to return Whale to your hand, then repeat.
    • Result: the energy breaks even, but you get unlimited enter, leave and cast triggers.
  • Adding Decoction Module (my own analysis, not listed by Spellbook): Module gives 1 energy per creature entering, doubled by Panharmonicon. That makes the Whale loop gain 2 energy each time, so it becomes infinite energy.
    • Payoffs: Whirler Virtuoso turns that into infinite flying Thopters. With Reckless Fireweaver out, each Thopter deals 1 damage to each opponent, twice with Panharmonicon, which wins the game. Infinite energy also makes Aetherwind Basker infinitely large.

Key engines:

  • Saheeli's copies: copies of creatures with "enters" effects are the deck's best value:
    • Duplicant: the exile is permanent even after the copy is sacrificed.
    • Territorial Aetherkite: energy plus damage to every other creature.
    • Whirler Rogue and Pia and Kiran Nalaar: 2 more Thopters each.
    • Combustible Gearhulk: draw 3 or damage.
    • Solemn Simulacrum: a land now, and a card when the copy is sacrificed.
    • Aethertide Whale: 6 energy.
  • Panharmonicon: doubles every "enters" trigger from artifacts and creatures, including Saheeli's copies.
  • Thopter makers: Sai, Thopter Spy Network, Whirler Virtuoso, Stridehangar Automaton (an extra Thopter whenever you make artifact tokens) and Retrofitter Foundry. Reckless Fireweaver turns every artifact entering into damage.
  • Energy payoffs: Nissa (cast permanents for 8 energy), Architect of the Untamed (6/6 for 8), Peema Trailblazer, Aetherworks Marvel and Era of Innovation. Aetheric Amplifier doubles your energy. Aetherflux Conduit's 50-energy ability lets you cast spells from a 7-card draw for free.

  • Ramp: about 14 (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Commander's Sphere, Talisman of Curiosity, Chromatic Lantern, Aetheric Amplifier, Cultivator's Caravan, Ornithopter of Paradise, Solar Transformer, Servant of the Conduit, Midnight Clock, Explosive Vegetation, Solemn Simulacrum, Bootleggers' Stash), plus Attune with Aether.
  • Card draw: about 11 (Glimmer of Genius, One with the Machine, Rogue Refiner, Thopter Spy Network, Sai, Elder Gargaroth, Peema Trailblazer, Era of Innovation, Bespoke Battlewagon, Combustible Gearhulk, Arcane Denial), plus Adaptive Omnitool and Aetherworks Marvel.
  • Targeted removal: 6 (Chaos Warp, Reality Shift, Duplicant, Confiscation Coup, Druid of Purification, Pia and Kiran Nalaar), plus 2 counterspells (Disallow, Arcane Denial).
  • Board wipes: 3 (Blasphemous Act, Chain Reaction, Aethersquall Ancient), plus Territorial Aetherkite.
  • Protection: Lightning Greaves, the 2 counterspells, and Rampaging Aetherhood's ward.

Ramp and draw are strong. Removal is a little light.

Nonland cards by mana value: 1: 4 | 2: 13 | 3: 15 | 4: 14 | 5: 5 | 6: 6 | 7+: 4. Average 3.67, the highest of the four decks. Heavy ramp supports it.

Colored symbols: blue 25, red 18, green 17, which is fairly balanced. Chromatic Lantern, Aether Hub, Spire of Industry and the three-color land fix it well.

sections.title: 5. Rules to know
sections.html:
• Energy counters belong to you, the player, not to a permanent. Paying energy is a cost, so it can't be responded to.
  • Saheeli's copy is a "when you do" trigger: you pay energy first, then choose the target.
    • The copy is a 5/5 artifact creature with haste, even if you copied a land, Vehicle or artifact. A copied Vehicle doesn't need crewing. A copied land can attack and tap for mana.
    • Copying one of your legendary permanents triggers the legend rule.
    • The copy is sacrificed at the next end step, so "dies" and "leaves" triggers happen then.
  • Extra combats (Lightning Runner): each extra combat has its own beginning-of-combat step, so Saheeli triggers again. You don't get an extra main phase.
  • Nissa's alternative cost: paying 8 energy replaces the mana cost. Commander tax still adds {2} per previous cast. You can't combine it with another alternative cost.
  • Panharmonicon only doubles triggers caused by an artifact or creature entering. It doesn't double "when you cast" triggers. It doesn't double landfall from normal lands, but it does for the artifact lands (Treasure Vault, Slagwoods Bridge, Tanglepool Bridge), which give Nissa 4 energy instead of 2.
  • Duplicant: the exiled card stays exiled for good. The copy's power and toughness come from the exiled card.
  • Disallow can counter activated and triggered abilities, not just spells.
  • Aethersquall Ancient returns all other creatures, including yours. Tokens returned to hand stop existing.
  • Midnight Clock shuffles your hand and graveyard into your library before you draw 7.

sections.title: 6. Power level
sections.html:
No Game Changers. It does contain a two-card infinite combo (Lightning Runner + Aetherwind Basker). Bracket 2 says "no intentional two-card infinite combos," and Wizards no longer automatically counts precons as Bracket 2.

It plays at Bracket 2 strength. Tell the table about the Runner + Basker combo, though. If you plan to go for it on purpose, treat the deck as Bracket 3.

sections.title: 7. Weak spots and swaps
sections.html:
Weak spots:

  • Light removal.
  • Slow if energy sources don't show up early.
  • Saheeli has only Lightning Greaves for protection.
  • Its two board wipes kill its own Thopters.

Swaps:

  • Bootleggers' Stash → Nature's Lore. Cheaper ramp, and the Forest enters untapped, so it triggers landfall for Nissa and Architect of the Untamed.
  • Chain Reaction → Beast Within. An instant answer to anything, instead of a wipe that kills your own board.
  • Midnight Clock → Talisman of Creativity. Faster blue-red mana.
  • Triplicate Titan → Padeem, Consul of Innovation. Gives your artifacts hexproof and draws cards. Triplicate Titan costs 9.

sections.title: 1. Summary
sections.html: Blue-red-white artifacts and counters. Inspirit is a Spacecraft you "station" by tapping your creatures. Once it reaches 8 counters it flies and makes all your other artifacts hexproof and indestructible. The deck stacks charge and +1/+1 counters on artifacts, then multiplies them with proliferate. It wins with Darksteel Reactor (20 counters = you win), Lux Artillery (10 damage to each opponent) or a big artifact army.

sections.title: 2. Key cards and combos
sections.html:
No infinite combos (checked on Commander Spellbook). Its main win lines:

  • Darksteel Reactor + proliferate: Reactor gains a counter each upkeep, and every proliferate adds another. Reaching 20 wins the game immediately at any moment, even mid-turn. Reactor is indestructible on its own.
  • Deepglow Skate: doubles every kind of counter on any number of permanents. A Reactor at 10+ goes to 20+, so you win on the spot. It also doubles Lux Artillery's count, Inspirit's charge counters and +1/+1 counters.
  • Lux Artillery: at your end step, if your artifacts and creatures have 30+ counters in total (charge and +1/+1 both count), it deals 10 damage to each opponent, every turn. It also gives your artifact creature spells sunburst.
  • Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus: every proliferate happens twice. It also triggers Kilo twice as often, in effect.
  • Kilo, Apogee Mind: proliferates whenever it becomes tapped, whether by attacking (it has haste), stationing Inspirit, or paying for improvise (Organic Extinction, Kappa Cannoneer, Universal Surveillance). Tapping Kilo to station Inspirit adds 3 charge counters plus a proliferate, and the proliferate resolves first.
  • Inspirit at 8+: protects your whole artifact board from targeted and "destroy" removal, including board wipes like Wrath of God. It doesn't stop exile, sacrifice, -X/-X or bounce.
  • Other counter engines: Steel Overseer, Coretapper, Surge Conductor (proliferate whenever a nontoken artifact enters), Resourceful Defense (moves counters off dying permanents), Moxite Refinery, Thrummingbird, Experimental Augury and Tezzeret's Gambit.
  • Big mana: Astral Cornucopia and Empowered Autogenerator grow with proliferate. Pentad Prism and Everflowing Chalice too.
  • Card draw: Insight Engine, Uthros Research Craft (draw for each artifact spell once stationed to 3), Jhoira (draw for each artifact or legendary spell) and Universal Surveillance.

sections.title: 3. Card balance (my count)
sections.html:
• Lands: 40, including 7 artifact lands.
  • Ramp: about 11 (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Pentad Prism, Everflowing Chalice, Astral Cornucopia, Empowered Autogenerator, Solar Array, Crystalline Crawler, Etherium Sculptor, Enthusiastic Mechanaut, Cloud Key).
  • Card draw: about 12 (Insight Engine, Uthros Research Craft, Thought Monitor, Universal Surveillance, Pull from Tomorrow, Tezzeret's Gambit, Thirst for Knowledge, Experimental Augury, Jhoira, Etched Oracle, Mindless Automaton, Long-Range Sensor).
  • Targeted removal: 6 (Swords to Plowshares, Dispatch, Chaos Warp, Lux Cannon, Angel of the Ruins, Alibou), plus Swan Song.
  • Board wipes: 3 (Fumigate, Organic Extinction, which spares your artifact creatures, and Chain Reaction).
  • Protection: Inspirit at 8+, Ripples of Potential (phase out), Swan Song, Resourceful Defense, indestructible Bridge lands, and Kappa Cannoneer's ward.

This is the best card draw of the four decks. Removal is on the light side.

sections.title: 4. Mana curve
sections.html:
Nonland cards by mana value (X counted as 0): 0: 3 | 1: 5 | 2: 12 | 3: 16 | 4: 12 | 5: 3 | 6: 2 | 7+: 6. Average 3.34. Cost reducers (Etherium Sculptor, Enthusiastic Mechanaut, Cloud Key) and improvise/affinity cards play cheaper than their printed costs.

Colored symbols: blue 26, white 13, red 11. Mostly blue. Inspirit itself needs all three colors.

sections.title: 5. Rules to know
sections.html:
• Station:
    • Tap another untapped creature you control to put charge counters on the Spacecraft equal to that creature's power.
    • Sorcery speed only.
    • Creatures that just arrived can be tapped for station. Station is the Spacecraft's own ability (CR 702.184a), and summoning sickness only stops a creature's own {T} abilities and attacks (CR 302.6). Confirmed 2026-10-10.
    • Each threshold ("1+", "8+") turns on once the counter count is reached. At 8+ Inspirit becomes an artifact creature.
  • Inspirit's 1+ ability targets "up to one other artifact" each combat. You choose a +1/+1 counter or two charge counters. Use charge counters on Darksteel Reactor or Lux Cannon.
  • Proliferate: choose any number of permanents and players that already have counters. Each gets one more of every kind it has. You can skip opponents' permanents.
  • Darksteel Reactor's win happens as soon as it has 20 counters (a "state trigger"). It doesn't wait for your upkeep. Opponents can respond only by removing counters or stopping the trigger.
  • Lux Artillery checks at the beginning of your end step. Charge and +1/+1 counters on your artifacts and creatures all count, including Inspirit's.
  • Phasing (Ripples of Potential): phased-out permanents are treated as if they don't exist until your next untap, so wipes miss them. Counters and Equipment stay with them.
  • Improvise lets you tap artifacts to pay generic mana. Tapping Kilo that way triggers its proliferate.
  • Phyrexian mana ({U/P}): you can pay 2 life instead of {U}. It still counts as blue for color identity.
  • Sunburst / converge count the different colors of mana spent, so pay with colored mana, not Sol Ring.
  • Inspirit isn't a creature below 8 counters, so it can't attack or deal commander damage until then.

sections.title: 6. Power level
sections.html: No Game Changers, no two-card infinite combos and no mass land denial. It fits Bracket 2 (Core). Darksteel Reactor and Lux Artillery wins can come out of nowhere, so mention them to new players.

sections.title: 7. Weak spots and swaps
sections.html:
Weak spots:

  • Inspirit needs creatures to tap, and only about 25 of the cards are creatures.
  • Before Inspirit reaches 8 counters, artifact wipes hurt badly.
  • Few counterspells.
  • Chain Reaction kills your own artifact creatures.

Swaps (all stay Bracket 2):

  • Thrummingbird → Flux Channeler. Proliferate on every noncreature spell, which is most of this deck, instead of needing combat damage.
  • Mindless Automaton → Inexorable Tide. Proliferate on every spell you cast.
  • Secluded Steppe → Inventors' Fair. A land that finds Darksteel Reactor, Lux Artillery or Steel Overseer when needed.

sections.title: 1. Summary
sections.html: Black-red-green lands deck. Hearthhull is a Spacecraft you station by tapping creatures. Once stationed, it sacrifices lands to draw cards. At 8+ counters it flies with haste, and every land you sacrifice makes each opponent lose 2 life. The deck ramps hard, sacrifices fetch-style lands, replays lands from the graveyard, and turns each land entering or dying into tokens, damage and extra combats.

sections.title: 2. Key cards and combos
sections.html:
Infinite loop (confirmed on Commander Spellbook):

  • The Gitrog Monster + Dakmor Salvage (two-card loop):
    • Setup: you need more cards in hand than your maximum hand size.
    • Loop: in your cleanup step, discard Dakmor Salvage. Gitrog makes you draw. Replace that draw with dredge 2 (mill 2, return Dakmor to hand). You're over hand size again, so repeat. Every land milled draws another card.
    • Result: you mill as much of your library as you like, but it doesn't win by itself. Dredge is optional, so you can stop at any point. Don't mill yourself out.
    • Payoffs: a full graveyard of lands powers Splendid Reclamation, Aftermath Analyst, Multani, Uurg, Centaur Vinecrasher and Formless Genesis.

Key engines:

  • Hearthhull at 8+ (commander): every land you sacrifice drains 2 from each opponent. Fetch-style lands each count once, including Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, Myriad Landscape, Escape Tunnel, Rocky Tar Pit, Mountain Valley, and the three Courtyard/Theater/Overlook lands. So do Harrow, Roiling Regrowth, Springbloom Druid, Evendo Brushrazer, Sprouting Goblin, Baloth Prime, Uurg and Gitrog's upkeep cost.
  • Szarel, Genesis Shepherd: play lands from your graveyard. You can replay the same fetch-style land every turn for repeated drains, landfall and Titania tokens. Szarel also puts +1/+1 counters on a creature whenever you sacrifice a nontoken permanent on your turn.
  • Titania, Protector of Argoth: a 5/3 Elemental whenever one of your lands goes to the graveyard from the battlefield. With Omnath, Locus of Rage, each of those Elementals deals 3 damage when it dies.
  • Landfall: Rampaging Baloths (4/4s), Omnath (5/5s), Tireless Tracker (Clues) and Moraug.
    • Moraug gives an extra combat for each land entering in your main phase.
    • A fetch-style land triggers landfall twice: once when it enters and once for the land it fetches.
  • Sacrifice payoffs:
    • Mayhem Devil: 1 damage whenever any player sacrifices anything.
    • Korvold: draws a card and grows on every sacrifice.
    • Juri and Mazirek grow on sacrifices.
    • Baloth Prime: a 4/4 per land sacrifice, and it untaps.
  • Hearthhull + Mayhem Devil + Titania: one fetch-style land sacrifice = 2 life from each opponent, 1 damage to any target, a 5/3 token, and landfall twice.
  • Planetary Annihilation: every player keeps six lands, sacrifices the rest, then all creatures take 6 damage.
    • Your sacrificed lands drain opponents through Hearthhull, and Mayhem Devil triggers for every land any player sacrifices.
    • Titania's tokens and Baloth Prime's Beasts are created after the damage, so they survive. Only cast it with Titania out and lots of lands.

sections.title: 3. Card balance (my count)
sections.html:
• Lands: 42. That's high, but lands are this deck's resource.
  • Ramp: about 13 (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Cultivate, Harrow, Roiling Regrowth, Skyshroud Claim, Springbloom Druid, Oracle of Mul Daya, Exploration Broodship, Augur of Autumn, Horizon Explorer), plus Evendo Brushrazer, Sprouting Goblin and Binding the Old Gods.
  • Card draw: about 11 (Hearthhull, The Gitrog Monster, Korvold, Tireless Tracker, Night's Whisper, Escape to the Wilds, Braids, God-Eternal Bontu, Eumidian Wastewaker, Sprouting Goblin, Soul of Windgrace).
  • Targeted removal: 9 (Infernal Grasp, Putrefy, Beast Within, Tear Asunder, Windgrace's Judgment, Binding the Old Gods, Rakdos Charm, World Breaker, Pest Infestation).
  • Board wipes: 3 (Blasphemous Act, Gaze of Granite, Planetary Annihilation).
  • Protection: almost none (only Soul of Windgrace can make itself indestructible).

This has the best removal of the four decks and the weakest protection.

sections.title: 4. Mana curve
sections.html:
Nonland cards by mana value (X counted as 0): 1: 4 | 2: 12 | 3: 18 | 4: 8 | 5: 9 | 6: 3 | 7+: 3. Average 3.51. Heavy ramp means 5-drops come down around turn 4.

Colored symbols: green 46, black 24, red 19. It's a green deck splashing black and red. Omnath needs {R}{R}{G}{G}. Most ramp spells only find basic lands, so keep enough Mountains and Swamps in the deck.

sections.title: 5. Rules to know
sections.html:
• Station works the same as on Inspirit: tap other creatures, sorcery speed, counters equal to their power. Hearthhull's 2+ ability needs only 2 counters and is the early card-draw engine. It only gives extra land drops on your own turn.
  • Hearthhull isn't a creature below 8 counters, so it can't attack or block until then. As an artifact, it dies to artifact removal.
  • Fetch-style lands are sacrificed as a cost, so triggers for "whenever you sacrifice a land" (Hearthhull, Baloth Prime, Mayhem Devil) and "land put into a graveyard" (Titania, Gitrog) all fire.
  • Moraug:
    • Landfall gives an extra combat phase but no extra main phase.
    • A land entering in your precombat main phase puts the extra combat before your normal one.
    • Your creatures untap at the start of each extra combat. Lands entering during combat don't trigger it.
  • Gitrog's upkeep: sacrifice a land or sacrifice Gitrog. The land sacrifice also triggers Gitrog's draw and Hearthhull's drain.
  • Dredge replaces a draw, and you choose each time. You can only dredge if you have at least 2 cards in your library.
  • Planetary Annihilation:
    • Players choose their six lands in turn order, then everyone sacrifices at the same time, then damage is dealt.
    • Triggers wait until it finishes resolving, then go on the stack in turn order.
    • Mayhem Devil's damage triggers still resolve even though the Devil died to the 6 damage, because the abilities exist on their own.
  • Szarel / Ramunap-style effects let you play a land from your graveyard. It still uses your land drop for the turn.
  • Aftermath Analyst and Splendid Reclamation return all lands tapped. Each one triggers landfall separately (many Omnath and Baloths tokens).

sections.title: 6. Power level
sections.html:
No Game Changers. It has a two-card loop (Gitrog + Dakmor Salvage), but the loop only mills and draws, so it doesn't win by itself.

Many playgroups treat Planetary Annihilation as mass land destruction, which the Bracket 1–3 guidelines say not to expect. Mention it before the game, or swap it out.

It plays at Bracket 2 (Core).

sections.title: 7. Weak spots and swaps
sections.html:
Weak spots:

  • Graveyard hate (an opponent's Bojuka Bog or Rest in Peace) shuts off Szarel, Gitrog and the land recursion.
  • Hearthhull is a slow artifact commander with no protection.
  • Few instant-speed answers.

Swaps (all stay Bracket 2):

  • Groundskeeper → Sylvan Safekeeper. A free, instant-speed land sacrifice that also protects a creature by giving it shroud. Each activation triggers Hearthhull, Titania, Mayhem Devil, Baloth Prime and Korvold.
  • Planetary Annihilation → Ramunap Excavator. Only if your group treats it as land destruction. Excavator backs up Szarel by letting you replay lands from the graveyard.
  • Wastes → Dryad of the Ilysian Grove. An extra land drop each turn, and it makes all your lands every basic type, which fixes Omnath's double red and green. The deck still has plenty of colorless mana for World Breaker.

comparison.title: Matchups
comparison.html:
• Living Energy has the highest ceiling. It's the only deck with a real two-card win (Lightning Runner + Aetherwind Basker), and Saheeli can produce huge turns. Its Thopter tokens fold to Eternal Might's Archfiend of Ifnir and to Chain Reaction or Blasphemous Act.
  • Counter Intelligence wins out of nowhere with Darksteel Reactor or Lux Artillery. Reactor is indestructible, so only exile, bounce or shuffle effects answer it:
    • Eternal Might: Cast Out, Despark, Angel of Sanctions.
    • Living Energy: Chaos Warp.
    • World Shaper: Tear Asunder, World Breaker. Its "destroy" removal, such as Beast Within, doesn't work on Reactor.

Everyone should hold an answer for it.

  • World Shaper has the most removal and handles the other decks' engines well. Its exile effects get around Inspirit's indestructible artifacts. It's weak to graveyard hate, and both Living Energy and Counter Intelligence play Soul-Guide Lantern.
  • Eternal Might is the grindiest. It keeps coming back from board wipes thanks to its graveyard. World Shaper's Bojuka Bog and Rakdos Charm (graveyard exile) are its biggest problems.

comparison.title: Keeping games fair
comparison.html:
All four play at about the same level (Bracket 2). Before playing, mention two things:

  • Living Energy contains the Lightning Runner + Aetherwind Basker infinite.
  • World Shaper contains Planetary Annihilation.

If one deck keeps winning, the suggested swaps in each file are small, Bracket-2-safe upgrades for the other decks.
